title: AWS Management Tools
description: Explore the AWS Console, CLI, CloudShell, SDKs, Free Tier, and pricing concepts.

data.text: AWS offers several tools to manage your cloud resources. The AWS Management Console is a web-based visual interface. The AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) lets you control services from the terminal. AWS CloudShell provides a browser-based shell. And the AWS SDKs let you write code that interacts with AWS in languages like Python, JavaScript, and Java.

cards.title: AWS Management Console
cards.description: A web-based point-and-click interface. Great for beginners and for visually exploring services.

cards.title: AWS CLI
cards.description: A unified command-line tool for managing AWS services from scripts or your terminal.

cards.title: AWS SDKs
cards.description: Libraries for programming languages like Python, JavaScript, Java, and Go that let you build applications on AWS.

data.text: The AWS CLI is one of the most powerful tools for managing AWS from the command line. After installing it and configuring your credentials with aws configure, you can run commands like the ones below.

data.title: Common AWS CLI Commands
data.content: These commands demonstrate how to list EC2 instances, create an S3 bucket, and check your AWS identity from the terminal.
data.code:
# List all EC2 instances in a Region
aws ec2 describe-instances \
  --query 'Reservations[*].Instances[*].[InstanceId,State.Name,InstanceType]' \
  --output table

# Create an S3 bucket
aws s3 mb s3://my-demo-bucket-12345 --region us-east-1

# List S3 buckets
aws s3 ls

# Check who you are authenticated as
aws sts get-caller-identity

data.text: AWS Free Tier and Pricing Concepts

AWS offers a Free Tier that lets you experiment with many services at no cost for 12 months. After that, or for services not covered by the Free Tier, you pay for what you use. AWS uses a pay-as-you-go model, which means you are billed based on actual usage rather than fixed monthly fees.

data.title: Key Pricing Concepts
items: Compute — Charged per second (or hour) based on instance type and duration.
Storage — Charged per gigabyte per month based on the amount of data stored.
Data Transfer — Charged when data moves between Regions or out to the internet. Transfer into AWS is free.
Requests — Charged per API call for services like S3 and DynamoDB.

terms.definition: A web-based visual interface for managing AWS services.
A command-line tool for managing AWS services from scripts or terminal sessions.
A program offering limited free usage of many AWS services for 12 months.
A pricing model where you pay only for the resources you consume, with no upfront commitment.

data.title: Python/Boto3 Example
data.content: You can also use the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3) to interact with AWS programmatically.
data.code:
import boto3

# Create a low-level S3 client
s3 = boto3.client('s3', region_name='us-east-1')

# List all S3 buckets
response = s3.list_buckets()
for bucket in response['Buckets']:
    print(f"Bucket: {bucket['Name']}")

# Upload a file
s3.upload_file('local-file.txt', 'my-demo-bucket', 'remote-file.txt')

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The Console is visual and great for beginners
The CLI is ideal for automation and scripting
SDKs let you build applications that integrate with AWS
AWS Free Tier lets you learn without cost for 12 months
Pay-as-you-go pricing means you only pay for what you use
